about.title: Gilroy Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Gilroy residents rely on all kinds of products every day, from farm and warehouse equipment tied to the area's agricultural roots to household appliances, vehicles, and tools used along corridors like Monterey Highway and US-101. When one of those products fails because of a design flaw, a manufacturing error, or a missing warning, the resulting injury can upend daily life fast. California law generally allows injured people to pursue a claim under strict liability, meaning the focus is on whether the product was defective and caused harm, not on proving the manufacturer was careless. That distinction matters for Gilroy families trying to understand their options after an incident. We handle product liability claims directly. Our team can review what happened, explain possible next steps, and help preserve the product itself, which is often the most important piece of evidence in these cases.

items.title: Strict Liability Can Simplify the Path Forward
items.desc: Because California often applies strict liability to defective products, injured people generally don't have to prove the manufacturer was negligent, just that the product was defective and caused harm.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can all potentially be held liable, which means there may be more than one avenue to pursue after a product injury in Gilroy.

items.title: Evidence Preservation Guidance From Day One
items.desc: Our team can advise on keeping the defective product intact and unaltered, since it's often central to establishing what went wrong.

items.question: Do I need to prove the manufacturer was careless?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California product liability claims often rely on strict liability, which focuses on whether the product itself was defective and caused injury. We can review the specifics of your situation to explain which legal theory may apply.

items.question: What should I do with the product that hurt me?
items.answer: Try to keep it in the same condition it was in when the injury happened, and avoid repairing or discarding it. The product is frequently the key piece of evidence in these claims, so preserving it can matter a great deal.
